_comment: Display config for Sri Lanka. Coherence-only (Level 1): no BTR / BER / NR7 data, so no btrMitigationSourceRef, countrySectors, or mitigationTaxonomy. Document taxonomy and provenance drive the dashboard with no code changes (same shape as panama-country-config.json).
name: Sri Lanka
_anchorDocTypeComment: Intentionally omitted. anchorDocType drives the Vision Anchor Coverage view, which treats one document as the country's north-star/long-term vision that every other doc operationalises (Mongolia: Vision 2050 = SECTORAL). Sri Lanka's corpus is three convention commitments (NDC / NBSAP / LDN) plus nine national sectoral policies, not a vision-and-derivatives hierarchy, so no anchor is set and that view stays off.
_documentTypesComment: Sri Lanka's twelve source documents, from data_sri_lanka_16Sep26.xlsx (18 Sep 2026 revision). This list REPLACES the previous eight-document corpus at the country office's instruction: the National Mineral Policy (NMP) and the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Policy (NFAP) are deliberately no longer included. shortLabel / fullLabel are verbatim from the xlsx Doc and Document columns; mediumLabel parentheticals name the sector domain, or for NDC/NBSAP/LDN the xlsx Convention column value. published / author / objective are verbatim from each document's own front matter (PDFs in the country office's Policies folder); fields a document does not state are omitted rather than inferred. Colors from the UNDP-compatible Tailwind palette; avoids reserved red (#dc2626 political sensitivity), BTR purple (#7c3aed), and OTHER grey (#78716c); twelve hues. The energy policy, at the centre of the flagged pairs, takes yellow rather than orange so its arcs stay clearly apart from the dashed misalignment red (CIE76 distance 57, not 23); the closest remaining document pair is about 21.
_docClassComment: Machine-readable document classification (docClass) and national-hierarchy level (docTier) consumed by src/lib/doc-taxonomy. THE VOCABULARY IS PROJECT-DEFINED (see DOC_CLASSES); EACH ASSIGNMENT TRACES TO THE DOCUMENT'S OWN SELF-DESCRIPTION recorded in docKind below, never its subject matter. NDC is a contribution declared to the UNFCCC and LDN declares country targets to the UNCCD (commitment, tier 2; no tier-1 instrument exists in this corpus, which has no unifying national vision document, so tier 1 is intentionally empty). NBSAP calls itself a Strategy and Action Plan and NEneP gazettes itself as 'Policy & Strategies' (sector_strategy, tier 3). NAgP, NEnvP, NWRP, NLTP, NTP, NPWM and NWP each self-describe as a national sectoral policy; the vocabulary's closest class is sector_plan (tier 3), and 'policy' vs 'plan' is noted as an approximation. NPPPP self-describes as the national physical planning policy and plan, a spatial planning instrument (territorial_instrument, tier 3 - national scope, unlike Panama's subnational PIOTA at tier 4). NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE COUNTRY OFFICE - confirm before this ships.

_targetProvenanceComment: Corpus rebuilt 2026-09-23 from data_sri_lanka_16Sep26.xlsx (18 Sep revision; raw cell-content sha256 58d49676bac836fa4ac70556751beaed57ccdd9c7d92e16bd23b97d2b9fbf80b), sheet targets_1, replacing the previous 404-target / 8-document corpus. 225 targets across 12 documents. The country office curated targets_1 by merging each statement together with its numbered sub-items; that merge is deliberate and the target SET is used exactly as delivered. Where the document itself supplies the statement as its own row in the companion sheet targets_0, the statement is the target text and the sub-items are carried as activities (NAgP 15, NEneP 10, NBSAP 16 targets; 383 activity lines). Where no such row exists (NEnvP's 27 section rows, NDC's 19 sector rows) the cell is left exactly as delivered, because the only alternative would be to cut a chapter heading out of the string and call it a target. NBSAP's 16 targets are unchanged from the previous corpus and its actions are the same content the office delivered on 17 Jul, so they are carried forward from commit 7006442, keeping the per-action section numbers, after asserting the content matches the new sheet. Text repair was conservative and evidence-based: zero-width spaces deleted (they sit inside words in this sheet), non-breaking spaces made ordinary, the private-use Symbol bullet U+F0B7 mapped to a bullet; and 170 run-together words separated, each only where the separated phrase appears in an independent source (the policy's own PDF text, the committed PPPP executive summary, or the previous corpus) and the joined form is not a word in the PDF or the dictionary. 45 targets are marked textCleanup 'cleaned'; the rest are verbatim. Two joined forms are kept because the published PDFs print them that way ('national wildlifepolicy' in NWP, 'strategic fuelreserves' in NEneP). The sheet labels one NEnvP section '4.3.'; its statements are numbered 4.3.1.n and the PDF numbers the section 4.3.1, so it is labelled 4.3.1. Ingest: dev_data_scripts/ingest_sri_lanka_16sep26.py (extracts PDF text at run time and aborts rather than skipping the repair), which imports decompose() from dev_data_scripts/decompose_sri_lanka_16sep26.py so the country-office review workbook and this corpus cannot drift. NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE COUNTRY OFFICE.
_docProvenanceComment: Primary-source citations per document. The xlsx Source column is populated for NBSAP rows only and holds a document reference rather than a URL, so no urls are invented; NDC's UNFCCC url is carried forward from the previous config. Titles, years, ministries and objectives are verbatim from each document's own front matter in the country office's Policies folder. The National Physical Planning Policy and Plan PDF is a scan with no extractable text, so its metadata is carried forward unchanged from the previous config's PPPP entry. LDN's published date and url are NOT carried forward from the previous config: the country office reports that the UNCCD site has since been updated and now publishes nine targets and one action, which is what this corpus carries, so the 2017 document reference no longer matches the data.
